blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE donning and doffing safety
stem: Why must healthcare personnel be trained to don and remove personal protective equipment (PPE) correctly?

options.A: Correct donning is needed for intended protection, and careful removal reduces self-contamination or occupational exposure from contaminated PPE surfaces.
options.B: PPE technique can be learned reliably by observation during routine care, so formal instruction is mainly useful for newly licensed personnel.
options.C: Training is primarily needed when a recognized outbreak is underway because routine-care PPE has little potential for self-contamination during removal.
options.D: Experienced staff can omit retraining when PPE products or workplace conditions change because prior clinical use establishes lasting competency.

rationale: A is correct. NIOSH states that donning means putting on and using PPE properly to achieve the intended protection and minimize exposure, while doffing means removing PPE in a way that avoids self-contamination. CDC occupational infection-prevention guidance lists how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE as required training content. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132 also requires PPE training and retraining when workplace changes, PPE changes, or demonstrated knowledge/skill gaps make prior training inadequate. B, C, and D therefore misstate the role and persistence of PPE competency.
educational_objective: Explain why correct PPE donning, doffing, and training are necessary to achieve intended protection and reduce occupational exposure or self-contamination.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (CDC/NIOSH); Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA); NCSBN
source_document_title: Donning and Doffing PPE: Proper Wearing, Removal, and Disposal; Occupational Infection Prevention and Control: Education and Training; 29 CFR 1910.132; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NIOSH PPE module last reviewed October 3, 2022 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; current CDC occupational training guidance and current OSHA 1910.132 live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NIOSH Donning and Doffing PPE: donning means proper PPE use to achieve intended protection and minimize exposure; doffing means removal in a way that avoids self-contamination. CDC Occupational Education and Training, Box 4: PPE training includes how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE. OSHA 1910.132(f)(1)-(3): required PPE training, demonstration of understanding/ability, and retraining when workplace or PPE changes render prior training obsolete or when skill/knowledge is inadequate.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC/NIOSH and OSHA guidance directly supports correct donning for intended protection, careful doffing to avoid self-contamination, formal PPE-use training, and retraining when prior competency is no longer adequate.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches NIOSH definitions and CDC/OSHA training requirements.
option_audit.B: Plausible experience-based misconception but safe PPE technique is required training content rather than merely intuitive learning.
option_audit.C: Plausible outbreak-focused misconception but PPE training applies to routine occupational exposure as well as outbreaks.
option_audit.D: Plausible experience-based exemption but OSHA requires retraining when workplace or PPE changes make prior training obsolete or competency is inadequate.
